questions.stem:
At 298 K , the mole percentage of $\mathrm{N_2(g)}$ in air is 80%. Water is in equilibrium with air at a pressure of 10 atm . What is the mole fraction of $\mathrm{N_2(g)}$ in water at 298 K ?
($\mathrm{K_H}$ for $\mathrm{N_2}$ is $6.5 \times 10^{7}$ mmHg)
questions.solution:
$$\mathrm{P_{N_2}} = 10 \times \frac{80}{100} = 8\ atm$$
$= 8 \times 760\ mm\,Hg$
$\mathrm{P_{N_2} = K_H \times x_{N_2}}$
$8 \times 760 = 6.5 \times 10^{7} \times \mathrm{x_{N_2}}$
$$\mathrm{x_{N_2}} = \frac{8 \times 760}{6.5 \times 10^{7}}$$
$= 9.35 \times 10^{-5}$

questions.stem: The heat of atomisation of methane and ethane are 'x' $\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ and 'y' $\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ respectively. The longest wavelength $(\lambda)$ of light capable of breaking the $\mathrm{C-C}$ bond can be expressed in SI unit as:
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{CH_4(g) \rightarrow C(g) + 4H}$
$\Delta H = x\ kJ/mol$
$$\mathrm{BE_{C-H}} = \frac{x}{4}\ kJ/mol$$
$\mathrm{CH_3-CH_3 \rightarrow 2C(g) + 6H(g)}$
$\Delta H = y\ kJ/mol$
[Structure of ethane drawn: $\mathrm{H_3C-CH_3}$ with all six C-H bonds and one C-C bond]
$\mathrm{BE_{C-C} + 6BE_{C-H}} = y$
$$\mathrm{BE_{C-C}} = y - 6 \times \frac{x}{4}\ kJ/mol$$
$$\frac{4y - 6x}{4}\ kJ/mol$$
$$\frac{4y - 6x}{4} \times 1000\ J/mol$$
$$250(4y - 6x) = \frac{hc}{\lambda} \times N_A$$
$$\lambda = \frac{hcN_A}{250(4y - 6x)}$$

questions.stem: The wavelength of spectral line obtained in the spectrum of $\mathrm{Li^{2+}}$ ion, when the transition takes place between two levels whose sum is 4 and difference is 2 , is
questions.solution:
3 + 1 = 4
3 - 1 = 2
$n_1 = 1$ | $n_2 = 3$
$$\frac{1}{\lambda} = R_H (Z)^{2}\left(\frac{1}{n_1^{2}} - \frac{1}{n_2^{2}}\right)$$
$$\frac{1}{\lambda} = R_H (3)^{2}\left(\frac{1}{1} - \frac{1}{9}\right) = R_H \times 9 \times \frac{8}{9} = 8R_H$$
$$\lambda = \frac{1}{8R_H} = \frac{1}{8} \times 912 = 114\ \mathrm{\mathring{A}}$$
$= 114 \times 10^{-8}$ cm
$= 1.14 \times 10^{-6}$

questions.stem:
Consider the following gaseous equilibrium in a closed container of volume 'V' at T(K).
$\mathrm{P_2(g) + Q_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2PQ(g)}$
2 moles each of $\mathrm{P_2(g)}$, $\mathrm{Q_2(g)}$ and $\mathrm{PQ(g)}$ are present at equilibrium. Now one mole each of '$\mathrm{P_2}$' and '$\mathrm{Q_2}$' are added to the equilibrium keeping the temperature at T(K). The number of moles of $\mathrm{P_2}$, $\mathrm{Q_2}$ and PQ at the new equilibrium, respectively, are
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{P_2(g) + Q_2(g) = 2PQ(g)}$
at eq : 2, 2, 2
$$k_{eq} = \frac{2^{2}}{2 \times 2} = 1$$
If one mol of each $\mathrm{P_2}$ & $\mathrm{Q_2}$ are added
eq. shifted in forward direction
$\mathrm{P_2 + Q_2 = 2PQ}$
$3 - x$ ; $3 - x$ ; $2 + 2x$
$k_{eq}$ remains same
$$\therefore \frac{(2 + 2x)^{2}}{(3 - x)^{2}} = 1$$
$$\frac{2 + 2x}{3 - x} = 1$$
$$x = \frac{1}{3}$$
$$n_P = 3 - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{8}{3} = 2.67$$
$$n_Q = 3 - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{8}{3} = 2.67$$
$$n_{PQ} = 2 + 2 \times \frac{1}{3} = \frac{8}{3} = 2.67$$

questions.stem:
Find out the statements which are not true.
A. Resonating structures with more number of covalent bonds and lesser charge separation are more stable.
B. In electromeric effect, an unsaturated system shows +E effect with nucleophile and -E effect with electrophile.
C. Inductive effect is responsible for high melting point, boiling point and dipole moment of polar compounds.
D. The greater the number of alkyl groups attached to the doubly bonded carbon atoms, higher is the heat of hydrogenation.
E. Stability of carbanion increases with the increase in $s-$ character of the carbon carrying the negative charge.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) R S with more number of covalent bonds and lesser charge separation will be more stable $\Rightarrow$ True
(B) $\mathrm{>C=O \xrightarrow{Nu^{\ominus}} >C(Nu)-O^-}$ (- E)
$\mathrm{>C=C< \xrightarrow{E^+} >C(E)-\overset{+}{C}<}$ (+ E)
(C) Due to Inductive effect polarity develop so BP | DM changes
(D) As no. of alkyl groups increases on double bond stability of alkene increases so HOH decreases.
$$\mathrm{HOH} \propto \frac{1}{\text{stability of alkene}}$$
(E) As % S character increas, the EN of carbon $\uparrow$
$\therefore$ - ve charge will be more stable on more EN carbon.

questions.stem:
The half-life of $\mathrm{^{65}Zn}$ is 245 days. After x days, 75% of original activity remained.
The value of x in days is ______ (Nearest integer)
(Given: log 3=0.4771 and log 2=0.3010)
questions.solution:
$t_{\frac{1}{2}} = 245$ days
75% of origional activity remained means on 25% of rection is completed
$$t_{x\%} = \frac{1}{K}\ln\frac{100}{100 - x}$$
$$K = \frac{\ln 2}{245}$$
$$t \times \frac{\ln 2}{245} = \ln\frac{100}{100 - 25} = \ln\frac{100}{75} = \ln\frac{4}{3}$$
$t = 101.675 \simeq 102$ day

questions.stem: 0.25 g of an organic compound "A" containing carbon, hydrogen and oxygen was analysed using the combustion method. There was an increase in mass of $\mathrm{CaCl_2}$ tube and potash tube at the end of the experiment. The amount was found to be 0.15 g and 0.1837 g , respectively. The percentage of oxygen in compound A is ______ %. (Nearest integer) (Given: molar mass in $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ H : 1, C : 12, O : 16 )

Molar conductivity of a weak acid HQ of concentration 0.18 M was found to be 1/30 of the molar conductivity of another weak acid HZ with concentration of 0.02 M . If $\lambda^{\circ}\mathrm{Q^-}$ happened to be equal with $\lambda^{\circ}\mathrm{Z^-}$, then the difference of the $\mathrm{pK_a}$ values of the two weak acids $(\mathrm{pK_a(HQ) - pK_a(HZ)})$ is ______ (Nearest integer).
[Given: degree of dissociation $(\alpha) \ll 1$ for both weak acids, $\lambda^{\circ}$ : limiting molar conductivity of ions]
questions.solution:
$K(HQ) = C_1\alpha_1^{2}$ ; $\alpha_1 = \dfrac{\lambda m(HQ)}{\lambda^{\circ} m(HQ)}$
$K(HZ) = C_2\alpha_1^{2}$ ; $\alpha_2 = \dfrac{\lambda m(HZ)}{\lambda^{\circ} m(HZ)}$
$$\frac{K(HQ)}{K(HZ)} = \frac{C_1}{C_2}\left(\frac{\alpha_1}{\alpha_2}\right)^{2} = \frac{0.18}{0.02}\left(\frac{\lambda m(HQ)}{\lambda m(HZ)}\right)^{2}$$
$$= 9\left(\frac{1}{30}\right)^{2} = \frac{1}{100}$$
$$-\log\left(\frac{K(HQ)}{K(HZ)}\right) = -\log\frac{1}{100}$$
$pk_a(HQ) - pk_a(HZ) = 2$
